info.title: slipwise API

get.description: Checks if a given username is available to be claimed.

post.description: Registers or updates a Firebase Cloud Messaging token for the authenticated user to receive push notifications.
Sends user feedback to the admin email.

Sends a 6-digit OTP to the user's email if they exist.
Returns 200 even if the user doesn't exist to prevent email enumeration.

429.description: requested too soon after the last one

post.description:
Returns 401 for both "no such user" and "wrong
password" — the same error either way, deliberately,
so a caller can't use this endpoint to enumerate which
emails are registered. An unverified account returns
403 separately, since at that point the password has
already confirmed the account exists.
post.summary: Log in with email and password

post.description:
Idempotent — revoking an already-invalid or
already-revoked token still returns 200, since from
the caller's point of view "logged out" is true
either way.

get.description:
Returns the public profile fields of the currently logged-in user.
Requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header.

patch.description:
Updates the authenticated user's profile fields.
Requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header.

post.description: Takes an ID Token from the mobile client and logs the user in, creating an account if necessary.
post.summary: Log in or sign up with Google

post.description:
The presented refresh token is revoked and a brand
new pair is issued, even though the request otherwise
succeeds — this bounds how long a stolen refresh
token remains useful past the legitimate user's next
refresh call.
post.summary: Rotate a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair

post.description:
Self-service escape hatch for an account stuck
mid-verification — used when the original code
expired (10 min) or was guessed wrong 3 times. Rate
limited to one send per 60 seconds per email so a
caller can't hammer the mail provider or the
recipient's inbox. The previous code is not
explicitly revoked; it simply stops being the
"latest" one once this issues a new one.

parameters.description: email to resend a code to
parameters.name: request

429.description: resend requested too soon after the last one

post.description: Validates the reset OTP and updates the user's password.

429.description: too many wrong attempts against this code

post.description:
Creates a user with email_verified_at = null and sends
a 6-digit OTP to the given email. The account cannot
log in until Verify is called with that code.

parameters.description: first name, last name, email, and password
parameters.name: request

400.description: missing required field, or password under 8 chars

post.description:
Checks the 6-digit code against the most recent
unused OTP for this email. On success, marks the
account verified and returns a usable token pair —
the caller is logged in immediately, no separate
Login call needed. Wrong-guess attempts count even on
failure; after 3 the code is dead regardless of
whether the next guess would've been right.
post.summary: Confirm signup OTP and activate the account

400.description: no active code, code expired, or code incorrect

429.description: too many wrong attempts against this code

get.description: Returns aggregated app-wide metrics (total users, tickets won/lost/pending, etc.)
Returns a paginated list of all registered users.

Retrieves a paginated list of all betting tickets tracked by the authenticated user.
The tickets are ordered by when they were tracked (most recent first).
Provides high-level details like the total odds and overall ticket status.

parameters.description: Delta sync timestamp (RFC3339). Returns only tickets updated after this time.
parameters.name: since

post.description:
Fetches the latest odds and selections for a given booking code
from the specified provider (e.g. SPORTYBET) directly.
This does NOT save the ticket to the user's history, it merely
resolves the code and allows them to preview it before tracking.
post.summary: Preview a betting ticket from a provider

400.description: Invalid provider, missing fields, or invalid code

500.description: External provider API failure or internal error

post.description:
Links a previously previewed ticket (via booking_code_id) to the authenticated user.
Optionally includes a stake and a description (e.g., "Weekend acca").
Once tracked, the system will actively poll this ticket for live status updates.

parameters.description: Booking code ID, stake, and optional description
parameters.name: request

get.description:
Fetches the deep details of a specific ticket tracked by the user.
This includes a breakdown of every single match/selection on the ticket,
including the live status of the matches and the current odds.

200.description: Detailed breakdown of the ticket's selections

delete.description:
Removes the link between the authenticated user and a specific ticket.
The underlying booking_code is not immediately deleted so that other users
tracking the same code are unaffected. A background job later sweeps orphaned codes.

patch.description: Update the stake or description of a tracked ticket.

get.description: Retrieves aggregated, materialized stats for the authenticated user (win/loss, ROI).

available.description: Available is true if the username is not taken.

error.description: Error is a short, user-displayable reason the request failed.

email.description: Email is the account's login identifier.

password.description: Password is the plaintext password to check against the stored hash.

refresh_token.description: RefreshToken is the token to revoke.

message.description: Message is a human-readable confirmation for the frontend to display.

id_token.description: IDToken is the JWT issued by the provider (e.g., Google or Apple).

refresh_token.description: RefreshToken is the token issued by a previous login/verify/refresh call.

email.description: Email identifies which account to send a fresh code to.
Email is the account's login identifier. Must be unique.

password.description:
Password is the plaintext password from the client; hashed
server-side before storage, never stored or logged as-is.

message.description: Message is a human-readable confirmation for the frontend to display.
message.example: account created, check your email for a verification code

access_token.description:
AccessToken is a short-lived (15 min) JWT sent as a Bearer token
on subsequent authenticated requests.

refresh_token.description:
RefreshToken is a long-lived (30 day) opaque token used only
against POST /auth/refresh to mint a new pair. It is rotated
(revoked and replaced) on every use.

email.description: Email is the user's email address.

id.description: ID is the user's unique identifier.

is_verified.description: IsVerified indicates whether the user has confirmed their email.

username.description: Username is the user's handle. Optional.

code.description: Code is the 6-digit OTP the user received by email.

email.description: Email identifies which account's OTP to check.

BearerAuth.description: Type "Bearer" followed by a space and the JWT access token.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
